items.title: Nepal, India finance ministers discuss post-flood reconstruction and economic ties
items.blurb: Talks covered reconstruction, trade, investment, energy and connectivity as Nepal seeks closer economic cooperation with India.

items.title: Bridges gone, roads damaged, villages cut off from relief
items.blurb: Helicopters and temporary crossings are helping deliver food and other essentials to cut-off communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, but officials say restoring roads and bridges must be an immediate priority.

items.title: India warns new US tariffs over Russian oil could hit ties, vows to protect energy security
items.blurb: New Delhi’s response could complicate already difficult trade negotiations with Washington, while refiners seek relief to manage existing Russian oil purchases.

items.title: Nepal Electricity Authority offers relief to families of flood-missing workers
items.blurb: Families of missing employees will receive Rs50,000 immediately, while relatives of permanent staff will get half their starting salary for up to six months.

items.title: Krishnabhir road reopens on Thursday
items.blurb: After 18 days of closure, a new track cut above the flood-damaged section is now carrying traffic in both directions.

items.title: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle reaches New Delhi
items.blurb: Wagle is set to meet his Indian counterparts and business leaders to discuss reconstruction and wider economic cooperation.

items.title: Climate change likely to have helped trigger Nepal glacier collapse, scientists say
items.blurb: Researchers say warming temperatures, thinning glaciers, thawing permafrost and excess meltwater likely created conditions that made the late-August collapse more likely.

items.title: Nuwakot substation destruction disrupts evacuation of 176.1 MW
items.blurb: Nepal Electricity Authority says disruption will exacerbate winter grid management.

items.title: Resolve legal hurdles to relief and property rights for families of the missing
items.blurb: Families of the missing face legal barriers to relief and property rights. The government must act now.

items.title: Families of missing foreign nationals want answers Nepal can’t give
items.blurb: Hundreds of foreigners remain unaccounted for as families press for cross-border searches, clearer information and official confirmation of their relatives’ status.

items.title: Five bodies found in flood-damaged Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
items.blurb: The discovery comes three weeks after devastating floods hit Rasuwa and left people missing inside the hydropower project.

items.title: Five bodies recovered from flood-hit Chilime hydropower project
items.blurb: Rescuers discovered the bodies while searching tunnels for people missing since the August 26 floods.

items.title: Three bodies recovered from flood-hit Chilime hydropower project three weeks later
items.blurb: Rescuers found the bodies inside a tunnel after the August 26 floods, with the search for additional victims continuing.

items.title: Timure was a bustling border hub. In hours, the floods wiped it off the map
items.blurb: More than 250 houses and other structures were swept away in the border settlement, leaving just six damaged houses standing and hundreds of people unaccounted for.

items.title: Bouldin meets Shah, offers US support for Nepal’s disaster recovery
items.blurb: The US chargé d’affaires expressed condolences over the Rasuwa floods as the prime minister called for greater global cooperation on climate-related risks.

items.title: Wagle to hold three high-level policy dialogues during India visit
items.blurb: Finance minister will engage Indian diplomats, business leaders and development policymakers, with flood reconstruction, investment, trade and connectivity expected to feature in his meetings.
